newsitem.title: UK: Britain's neighbourhood chemist seen under threat.
newsitem.headline: Britain's neighbourhood chemist seen under threat.

text.p: The future of Britain's neighbourhood chemist could be under threat if long-standing price controls on over the counter medicines are scrapped and if the government continues to cut fees for prescription drugs.

A new report from retail analysts Verdict Research published on Monday said small chemists were relying more heavily on revenue from prescription fees because superstores were taking an increasing share of toiletries and over the counter medicines.
"Their retail business is declining as superstores take an increasing share of toiletries and OTC medicine sales," it said.

Verdict said the prescription drug business might make up for the loss of toiletries sales, but "the profit impact is potentially devastating as gross margins on health and beauty products are almost twice those of NHS (National Health Service) prescribing."

The report argues that if the government wants to preserve local pharmacies it should be prepared to subsidise them directly via prescription fees rather than the indirectly through the price controls or Resale Price Maintenance system now under review.
It said the government was looking into expanding the role of the pharmacist as a first point of call for healthcare as a way of keeping the pharmacies in business.
In the health and beauty market, Verdict said Boots Co Plc and The Body Shop Plc were the dominant players, both with strong band names and products exclusive to their stores.

But it acknowledged that supermarkets -- like Tesco Plc and J. Sainsbury Plc -- continued to make major inroads into health and beauty retailing and it saw this area as a likely target for a price war.
"The high gross margins on these products and the supermarkets' inability to add value and gain share in this sector any other way make this a distinct possibility."
